newsitem.title: UK: Ecuador dips further as Bradys wait for U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador dips further as Bradys wait for U.S. data.

text.p: Ecuador Brady bonds took another hit on Friday, dragged down by concerns over the country's political chaos.
Traders said the rest of the market was slightly softer as the focus moves onto this afternoon's U.S. non-farm payroll data.
Ecuador Bradys dropped another point this morning after Congress voted to oust President Abdala Bucaram who in turn refused to go.
Vice-president Rosalia Arteaga had also staked a claim to the job, which Congress passed to their leader Fabian Alaracon.
The military, so far neutral, has called for a quick solution to the crisis but warned that the wait could not go on for too long.
"I think the selling is going to continue," one U.S. banker said.
The debt is not normally traded much in London, and traders are waiting to see how New York reacts next to the events. On Thursday, it sent Ecuador's Bradys more than two points lower.
ANZ economist Jerome Booth said the debt was probably a buy at these low levels, predicting reasonable economic prospects for Ecuador in the longer term.
However, investors are likely to be in for a bumpy ride in the short-term, he added.
There is more widespread concern that Ecuador's problems may be the catalyst which finally forces a more general correction in the Brady market's relentless rise since last year.
Spreads over U.S. Treasuries are around their lowest levels on record and one trader said there could be some heavy profit-taking in the more high-yield assets.
"People are going to start realising why these assets carry such high yields," he said, pointing to the recent tumble in Bulgarian Brady prices on its politicial and economic crisis.
The market overall is about 1/8 to 1/4 of a point lower as investors juggle positions ahead of the U.S. figures and the weekend, traders said.
